outcome: Universal acquired resistance ~9-12 mo; ~50-60% carry EGFR T790M gatekeeper mutation
resistance_mechanism: EGFR T790M gatekeeper substitution restores ATP affinity and sterically blocks drug binding
citation: Kobayashi S et al. N Engl J Med 2005;352:786-792, PMID 15737014; Pao W et al. PLoS Med 2005;2:e73

outcome: Acquired resistance with tertiary EGFR C797S; loss of covalent binding site
resistance_mechanism: EGFR C797S abolishes covalent cysteine bond required by osimertinib; cis/trans with T790M dictates options
citation: Thress KS et al. Nat Med 2015;21:560-562, PMID 25939061

outcome: ~20% of acquired resistance driven by focal MET amplification (bypass track)
resistance_mechanism: MET amplification reactivates PI3K/AKT via ERBB3 (HER3), bypassing EGFR blockade
citation: Engelman JA et al. Science 2007;316:1039-1043, PMID 17463250

outcome: HER2 (ERBB2) amplification a mutually-exclusive bypass mechanism to T790M
resistance_mechanism: ERBB2 amplification sustains downstream signaling independent of EGFR inhibition
citation: Takezawa K et al. Cancer Discov 2012;2:922-933, PMID 22956644

outcome: Subset of resistant tumors transform to small-cell lung cancer or undergo EMT
resistance_mechanism: Lineage plasticity: adeno-to-SCLC transformation (RB1/TP53 loss) and EMT escape EGFR dependence
citation: Sequist LV et al. Sci Transl Med 2011;3:75ra26, PMID 21430269

outcome: ALK G1202R solvent-front mutation dominant on-target resistance to 2nd-gen ALK TKIs
resistance_mechanism: ALK G1202R solvent-front substitution reduces inhibitor binding; bypass via EGFR/MET/KIT in others
citation: Gainor JF et al. Cancer Discov 2016;6:1118-1133, PMID 27432227

outcome: Acquired ROS1 G2032R solvent-front mutation confers crizotinib resistance
resistance_mechanism: ROS1 G2032R sterically hinders crizotinib binding (analogous to ALK G1202R)
citation: Awad MM et al. N Engl J Med 2013;368:2395-2401, PMID 23724914

outcome: Acquired resistance via MAPK-pathway reactivation without gatekeeper mutation
resistance_mechanism: RTK upregulation (PDGFRB) or NRAS mutation reactivates MEK/ERK, bypassing BRAF inhibition
citation: Nazarian R et al. Nature 2010;468:973-977, PMID 21107323

outcome: Response rate only ~5% - dramatically lower than melanoma; landmark tissue-context failure
resistance_mechanism: BRAF inhibition triggers rapid feedback reactivation of EGFR (high basal EGFR in colon epithelium) restoring MAPK signaling
citation: Prahallad A et al. Nature 2012;483:100-103, PMID 22281684; Kopetz S et al. J Clin Oncol 2015;33:4032-4038, PMID 26460303

outcome: Putative resistance mechanisms in 45% of progressors; often polyclonal
resistance_mechanism: Secondary KRAS pocket mutations (Y96C, H95, R68S), acquired trans-allele KRAS mutations, and RTK/MAPK bypass (MET amp, RAS/RAF/MEK, EGFR)
citation: Awad MM et al. N Engl J Med 2021;384:2382-2393, PMID 34161704

outcome: Improved PFS vs docetaxel but no OS benefit; short-lived responses
resistance_mechanism: Adaptive RTK/wild-type-RAS feedback reactivation and acquired bypass alterations blunt durability
citation: de Langen AJ et al. Lancet 2023;401:733-746, PMID 36764316

outcome: No benefit in KRAS-mutant tumors; benefit confined to KRAS wild-type - biomarker-defining trial
resistance_mechanism: Constitutive downstream KRAS activation makes upstream EGFR blockade irrelevant (intrinsic resistance)
citation: Karapetis CS et al. N Engl J Med 2008;359:1757-1765, PMID 18946061

outcome: PFS HR ~0.99 in KRAS-mutant vs 0.45 in wild-type - no efficacy in mutant subgroup
resistance_mechanism: Downstream KRAS mutation uncouples response from EGFR inhibition
citation: Amado RG et al. J Clin Oncol 2008;26:1626-1634, PMID 18316791

outcome: Did not prolong disease-free survival; early on-treatment benefit fully lost by 3 yr
resistance_mechanism: Transient anti-angiogenic effect only during dosing; VEGF blockade does not eradicate micrometastatic disease (angiogenic rebound/redundancy)
citation: Allegra CJ et al. J Clin Oncol 2011;29:11-16, PMID 20940184

outcome: Prolonged PFS (10.6 vs 6.2 mo) but NO OS benefit (16.8 vs 16.7 mo)
resistance_mechanism: Vascular normalization/pseudoresponse improves imaging PFS without altering tumor biology; adaptive angiogenic escape
citation: Chinot OL et al. N Engl J Med 2014;370:709-722, PMID 24552317

outcome: No OS benefit (15.7 vs 16.1 mo); greater neurocognitive decline with bevacizumab
resistance_mechanism: PFS/OS discordance plus on-mechanism neurocognitive/QoL harm; no durable disease control
citation: Gilbert MR et al. N Engl J Med 2014;370:699-708, PMID 24552318

target_mechanism: Marketed as a 'PARP inhibitor' (in fact not a bona fide PARP1 catalytic inhibitor)
outcome: Failed co-primary OS and PFS after positive phase II - famous false-positive
resistance_mechanism: Iniparib is not a true PARP inhibitor (non-selective cysteine-adduct compound); the presumed mechanism never existed
citation: O'Shaughnessy J et al. J Clin Oncol 2014;32:3840-3847, PMID 25185099; Patel AG et al. Clin Cancer Res 2012, PMID 22496272

target_mechanism: PARP1/2 catalytic inhibitor + trapping (synthetic lethality in HR-deficient tumors)
outcome: Acquired resistance via secondary/reversion mutations restoring BRCA reading frame
resistance_mechanism: Secondary intragenic BRCA2/BRCA1 mutations restore open reading frame and homologous recombination, re-establishing DNA repair
citation: Sakai W et al. Nature 2008;451:1116-1120, PMID 18264087

outcome: Stopped early for futility plus excess SAEs and treatment-related deaths; no OS improvement
resistance_mechanism: IGF-1R a non-validated target (correlate, not driver); IR/IGF-1R hybrid signaling and hyperglycemia toxicity
citation: Langer CJ et al. J Clin Oncol 2014;32:2059-2066, PMID 24888810

outcome: Stopped for futility; OS numerically worse in onartuzumab arm (HR 1.27); phase II signal not reproduced
resistance_mechanism: MET-IHC positivity a poor predictive biomarker (correlate, not oncogenic driver); enriched population still non-responsive
citation: Spigel DR et al. J Clin Oncol 2017;35:412-420, PMID 27937096

outcome: No PFS or OS improvement over docetaxel despite KRAS selection; phase II not confirmed
resistance_mechanism: MEK inhibition alone triggers RTK/RAS feedback reactivation of ERK; KRAS status insufficient to confer MEK dependence
citation: Janne PA et al. JAMA 2017;317:1844-1853, PMID 28492898

outcome: No significant OS benefit vs placebo in unselected pretreated NSCLC; led to FDA use-restriction
resistance_mechanism: Population not enriched for EGFR mutations - responsive subgroup (never-smokers, Asian) diluted below detectability
citation: Thatcher N et al. Lancet 2005;366:1527-1537, PMID 16257339

outcome: Acquired ESR1 ligand-binding-domain mutations after AI therapy drive endocrine resistance
resistance_mechanism: ESR1 Y537S / D538G render estrogen receptor constitutively active (ligand-independent), bypassing estrogen deprivation
citation: Toy W et al. Nat Genet 2013;45:1439-1445, PMID 24185512; Robinson DR et al. Nat Genet 2013;45:1446-1451, PMID 24185510

outcome: Acquired resistance associated with RB1 loss and cell-cycle bypass
resistance_mechanism: RB1 loss removes CDK4/6-blockade substrate; CCNE1/CDK6 amplification and CDK2 activation bypass the checkpoint
citation: Condorelli R et al. Ann Oncol 2018;29:640-645, PMID 29236940; O'Leary B et al. Cancer Discov 2018

outcome: Primary and acquired resistance via PI3K-pathway activation
resistance_mechanism: PTEN loss / PIK3CA activating mutations sustain PI3K/AKT downstream of HER2; p95HER2 truncation lacks trastuzumab epitope
citation: Nagata Y et al. Cancer Cell 2004;6:117-127, PMID 15324695

outcome: Did not significantly improve overall survival in HER2+ advanced gastric cancer
resistance_mechanism: HER2 heterogeneity/lower amplification in gastric vs breast; co-amplified bypass RTKs (MET, EGFR, CCNE1) blunt HER2 dependence
citation: Hecht JR et al. J Clin Oncol 2016;34:443-451, PMID 26628478

outcome: Statistically modest PFS gain outweighed by severe toxicity (mood disorders, transaminitis); program abandoned
resistance_mechanism: Pan-PI3K inhibition non-selective - on-mechanism CNS/hepatic toxicity limits dosing; feedback RTK/AKT reactivation limits efficacy
citation: Di Leo A et al. Lancet Oncol 2018;19:87-100, PMID 29804902

outcome: No OS benefit in overall population; benefit only in AFP-high subgroup (later confirmed in REACH-2)
resistance_mechanism: Anti-angiogenic effect meaningful only in a biologically defined (AFP-high) subset - unselected population dilutes signal
citation: Zhu AX et al. Lancet Oncol 2015;16:859-870, PMID 25795410

outcome: Did not meet the OS primary endpoint
resistance_mechanism: Angiogenic redundancy - blocking VEGFR alone bypassed by alternative pro-angiogenic ligands (FGF, PlGF)
citation: Scagliotti GV et al. J Clin Oncol 2012;30:2829-2836, PMID 22753918

outcome: No OS benefit; program failed
resistance_mechanism: Tivantinib acts largely via non-MET cytotoxic (tubulin/anti-mitotic) effects - the presumed MET mechanism was not operative
citation: Scagliotti G et al. J Clin Oncol 2015;33:2667-2674, PMID 26134280

outcome: Halted early - worse outcomes than gemcitabine alone (detrimental effect)
resistance_mechanism: Stromal/Hedgehog depletion removed a restraining desmoplastic barrier, paradoxically accelerating progression
citation: Infinity halt (2012); Rhim AD et al. Cancer Cell 2014 / Ozdemir BC et al. Cancer Cell 2014

trial: Randomized phase II vismodegib in mCRC
outcome: No improvement in PFS or response; Hedgehog blockade added toxicity without benefit
resistance_mechanism: Hedgehog signaling not a driver in colorectal carcinoma (paracrine/correlative only)
citation: Berlin J et al. Clin Cancer Res 2013;19:258-267, PMID 23172884

outcome: Cutaneous squamous-cell carcinomas / keratoacanthomas in ~15-25% of patients
resistance_mechanism: Paradoxical MAPK activation: BRAF inhibitor drives RAF dimerization and ERK signaling in RAS-mutant keratinocytes - rationale for adding MEK inhibitor
citation: Su F et al. N Engl J Med 2012;366:207-215, PMID 22256804

outcome: Intrinsic (primary) resistance - exon-20 insertions do not respond to classical EGFR TKIs
resistance_mechanism: C-helix insertions constrain the ATP pocket into active conformation without enlarging the drug cleft, precluding TKI binding
citation: Yasuda H et al. Sci Transl Med 2013;5:216ra177, PMID 24353160

outcome: Acquired resistance dominated by heterogeneous secondary KIT kinase-domain mutations
resistance_mechanism: Secondary KIT mutations in ATP-binding pocket (exon 13/14) or activation loop (exon 17/18) restore kinase activity; polyclonal across lesions
citation: Heinrich MC et al. J Clin Oncol 2006;24:4764-4774, PMID 16954519; Antonescu CR et al. Clin Cancer Res 2005

outcome: AR-V7-positive patients show minimal PSA/response and inferior survival on AR-targeted agents
resistance_mechanism: AR-V7 splice variant lacks the ligand-binding domain (constitutively active, drug-insensitive); AR point mutations and neuroendocrine lineage plasticity
citation: Antonarakis ES et al. N Engl J Med 2014;371:1028-1038, PMID 25184630

outcome: Acquired AR point mutations convert antagonists into agonists
resistance_mechanism: AR F877L confers enzalutamide/apalutamide agonism; AR L702H and T878A broaden ligand promiscuity
citation: Joseph JD et al. Cancer Discov 2013;3:1020-1029, PMID 23779130

outcome: Acquired polyclonal FGFR2 kinase-domain mutations at progression
resistance_mechanism: FGFR2 gatekeeper (V564F/V565F) and molecular-brake/activation-loop mutations reduce inhibitor affinity; polyclonal on-target escape
citation: Goyal L et al. Cancer Discov 2017;7:252-263, PMID 28034880

outcome: Improved PFS but no OS benefit; FDA accelerated approval later withdrawn (2011) - landmark endpoint-discordance case
resistance_mechanism: PFS gain not translated to survival; adaptive angiogenic escape and lack of predictive biomarker
citation: Miller K et al. N Engl J Med 2007;357:2666-2676, PMID 18160686

outcome: ~1/3 of crizotinib resistance is ALK-independent (bypass-track activation)
resistance_mechanism: Bypass signaling via EGFR, KIT, or IGF-1R activation maintains downstream survival independent of ALK inhibition
citation: Katayama R et al. Sci Transl Med 2012;4:120ra17, PMID 22277784

outcome: Phase 3 negative: ipilimumab after radiotherapy did not significantly improve overall survival vs placebo in post-docetaxel mCRPC (HR 0.85, p=0.053).
resistance_mechanism: Immunologically 'cold', T-cell-excluded prostate tumor microenvironment with low tumor mutational burden and scant CD8 infiltration; checkpoint release insufficient without pre-existing anti-tumor T cells.
citation: Kwon EM et al. Lancet Oncol 2014;15:700-712. PMID 24831977

outcome: Phase 3 negative: ipilimumab monotherapy did not improve overall survival vs placebo in chemo-naive mCRPC (HR 1.11).
resistance_mechanism: Same cold, immune-excluded prostate TME; absence of pre-existing tumor-reactive T cells to be de-repressed by CTLA-4 blockade.
citation: Beer TM et al. J Clin Oncol 2017;35:40-47. PMID 27918725

outcome: Phase 3 negative: tremelimumab did not improve overall survival vs standard chemotherapy (dacarbazine/temozolomide) first-line; stopped for futility.
resistance_mechanism: OS endpoint confounded by crossover/subsequent CTLA-4 access and slow immune kinetics; monotherapy CTLA-4 activity insufficient vs chemotherapy comparator.
citation: Ribas A et al. J Clin Oncol 2013;31:616-622. PMID 23295794

outcome: Phase 3 negative: atezolizumab did not improve OS vs chemotherapy in the pre-specified PD-L1 IC2/3 primary population (HR 0.87, p=0.41), halting hierarchical testing.
resistance_mechanism: PD-L1 IHC selection failed to enrich for benefit; biomarker was a weak correlate, and the immune-excluded/depleted phenotype in the selected subgroup was not reversed by PD-L1 blockade.
citation: Powles T et al. Lancet 2018;391:748-757. PMID 29268948

outcome: Objective response 0% in mismatch-repair-proficient (MSS) CRC vs 40% in MMR-deficient tumors; established that MSS CRC does not respond to PD-1 blockade.
resistance_mechanism: Low tumor mutational burden -> few neoantigens, minimal T-cell infiltration; immunologically cold tumor without targets for reinvigorated T cells.
citation: Le DT et al. N Engl J Med 2015;372:2509-2520. PMID 26028255

outcome: No RECIST responders among 27 patients (one delayed response); single-agent checkpoint blockade inactive in pancreatic cancer.
resistance_mechanism: Dense desmoplastic/fibrotic stroma with myeloid (TAM/MDSC) exclusion of T cells, low TMB; profoundly immune-excluded microenvironment.
citation: Royal RE et al. J Immunother 2010;33:828-833. PMID 20842054

outcome: Phase 3 negative: nivolumab did not improve OS vs bevacizumab in recurrent GBM (median OS 9.8 vs 10.0 mo; HR 1.04).
resistance_mechanism: Low TMB, T-cell-excluded and profoundly immunosuppressive CNS microenvironment; corticosteroid use and blood-brain barrier further blunt immune response.
citation: Reardon DA et al. JAMA Oncol 2020;6:1003-1010. PMID 32437507

target_mechanism: Anti-PD-1 checkpoint blockade added to chemoradiation
outcome: Phase 3 negative: adding nivolumab to standard RT+TMZ did not improve PFS or OS in MGMT-methylated newly diagnosed GBM.
resistance_mechanism: Cold GBM microenvironment plus systemic/local immunosuppression; PD-1 blockade added without a rational combination to overcome T-cell exclusion.
citation: Lim M et al. Neuro-Oncol 2022;24:1935-1949. PMID (verify - unresolved)

outcome: Phase 3 negative: nivolumab + RT did not improve OS vs temozolomide + RT in MGMT-unmethylated GBM (HR 1.31 unfavorable).
resistance_mechanism: Immune-excluded, low-TMB GBM; substituting an inactive checkpoint agent for effective chemotherapy removed benefit.
citation: Omuro A et al. Neuro-Oncol 2023;25:123-134. PMID (verify - unresolved)

target_mechanism: IDO1 enzyme inhibition combined with anti-PD-1 blockade
outcome: Phase 3 negative: adding epacadostat to pembrolizumab did not improve PFS or OS vs pembrolizumab + placebo.
resistance_mechanism: IDO1 was a correlate of an inflamed tumor rather than a non-redundant driver of resistance; dose likely insufficient and kynurenine pathway redundant, so IDO1 inhibition added no benefit.
citation: Long GV et al. Lancet Oncol 2019;20:1083-1097. PMID 31221619

cancer_type: Resected MAGE-A3-positive non-small cell lung cancer (adjuvant)
outcome: Phase 3 negative: no improvement in disease-free survival vs placebo overall or in any subgroup; no predictive gene signature identified.
resistance_mechanism: Antigen expression was a correlate, not a driver; vaccine-induced antibody/T-cell responses did not translate to tumor rejection, and no gene-expression signature could stratify responders.
citation: Vansteenkiste JF et al. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:822-835. PMID 26765324

outcome: Phase 3 negative: no improvement in disease-free survival; predefined gene-expression signature also failed to identify a benefiting subgroup.
resistance_mechanism: MAGE-A3 vaccination generated humoral/cellular responses that were not tumor-protective; target antigen a passenger correlate rather than a causal dependency.
citation: Dreno B et al. Lancet Oncol 2018;19:916-929. PMID 30078459

outcome: Phase 3 negative: no OS benefit vs control (median OS 20.1 vs 20.0 mo); stopped for futility.
resistance_mechanism: Antigen escape: EGFRvIII is heterogeneously/clonally expressed and was lost in ~60% of recurrences (including many control tumors), so targeting it drove outgrowth of EGFRvIII-negative clones.
citation: Weller M et al. Lancet Oncol 2017;18:1373-1385. PMID 28844499

cancer_type: Unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer
outcome: Phase 3 negative: no OS improvement vs placebo overall (median OS 25.6 vs 22.3 mo, HR 0.88, NS); benefit only in an unplanned concurrent-chemoradiation subgroup.
resistance_mechanism: MUC1 vaccination did not induce protective immunity in the overall population; apparent subgroup effect reflects population heterogeneity rather than a validated driver.
citation: Butts C et al. Lancet Oncol 2014;15:59-68. PMID 24525013

cancer_type: Asymptomatic/minimally symptomatic metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
target_mechanism: Vaccinia/fowlpox PSA + TRICOM viral vector vaccine
outcome: Phase 3 negative: neither PROSTVAC nor PROSTVAC+GM-CSF improved OS vs placebo; stopped for futility.
resistance_mechanism: Immune-excluded prostate TME and immunosuppressive myeloid infiltrate; vaccine-induced PSA-specific T cells insufficient to overcome tolerance, despite an earlier phase 2 OS signal that did not replicate.
citation: Gulley JL et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:1051-1061. PMID 30521405

cancer_type: Asymptomatic chemo-naive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
outcome: Phase 3 terminated for futility: interim analysis showed <30% probability of meeting the OS endpoint vs docetaxel/prednisone.
resistance_mechanism: Whole-cell vaccine failed to generate protective immunity in the cold prostate TME; no OS advantage over cytotoxic chemotherapy.
citation: Cell Genesys VITAL-1 termination (2008); reviewed in Madan RA & Gulley JL, Curr Opin Urol 2011. PMID (verify - unresolved)

target_mechanism: Allogeneic GM-CSF-transduced tumor cell vaccine combined with chemotherapy
outcome: Phase 3 terminated early: unfavorable death imbalance (67 deaths GVAX+docetaxel vs 47 docetaxel control); no benefit and possible harm.
resistance_mechanism: Empiric vaccine+chemotherapy combination lacked mechanistic rationale; docetaxel dose reduction in the combination arm plus excess deaths signaled net harm.
citation: Cell Genesys VITAL-2 termination (2008); Small EJ et al. reviewed in Drake CG, Nat Rev Immunol 2010. PMID (verify - unresolved)

cancer_type: Treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma
target_mechanism: HLA-A*02-restricted multipeptide vaccine + GM-CSF/cyclophosphamide with TKI
outcome: Phase 3 negative: adding IMA901 to sunitinib did not improve OS (HR 1.34, p=0.087, numerically worse).
resistance_mechanism: Vaccine-induced immune-response magnitude was too low to matter; tumor-associated (self) antigens were correlates of expression, not protective targets, and concurrent sunitinib did not rescue potency.
citation: Rini BI et al. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:1599-1611. PMID 27720136

cancer_type: Advanced non-small cell lung cancer (maintenance after front-line chemo)
drug: Belagenpumatucel-L (Lucanix, TGF-beta2-antisense allogeneic tumor cell vaccine)
target_mechanism: Allogeneic whole-cell vaccine with TGF-beta2 antisense to reduce immunosuppression
outcome: Phase 3 negative: no OS difference vs placebo (20.3 vs 17.8 mo, HR 0.94, NS); only a post-hoc early-randomization/prior-radiation subgroup suggested benefit.
resistance_mechanism: Whole-cell vaccine failed to overcome NSCLC immune evasion; TGF-beta2 knockdown alone insufficient against redundant immunosuppressive pathways.
citation: Giaccone G et al. Eur J Cancer 2015;51:2321-2329. PMID 26283035

outcome: Randomized placebo-controlled phase 2b negative: tremelimumab did not improve OS vs placebo (median OS 7.7 vs 7.3 mo, HR 0.92).
resistance_mechanism: Mesothelioma is immunologically cold with a suppressive myeloid/mesothelial TME; single-agent CTLA-4 blockade could not generate effective anti-tumor immunity.
citation: Maio M et al. Lancet Oncol 2017;18:1261-1273. PMID 28729154

cancer_type: Recurrent high-grade glioma (glioblastoma/anaplastic astrocytoma) at resection
target_mechanism: Retroviral replicating vector delivering cytosine deaminase for local 5-FU conversion + immune activation
outcome: Phase 3 negative: no OS improvement vs standard of care (11.1 vs 12.2 mo, HR 1.06, p=0.62); all secondary endpoints negative.
resistance_mechanism: Insufficient/heterogeneous vector spread and prodrug conversion in a bulky immunosuppressed CNS tumor; immune activation inadequate against cold GBM.
citation: Cloughesy TF et al. JAMA Oncol 2020 (Toca 5). PMID (verify - unresolved)

target_mechanism: GM-CSF-armed oncolytic vaccinia virus (sequential with TKI)
outcome: Phase 3 terminated for futility: sequential Pexa-Vec then sorafenib did not improve OS and trended worse than sorafenib alone.
resistance_mechanism: Sequential oncolytic-virus-then-TKI design lacked rationale; intratumoral virus delivery/anti-viral immunity did not translate to systemic tumor control, and delaying effective sorafenib was detrimental.
citation: Abou-Alfa GK et al. Liver Cancer 2024;13:256-264. PMID 38756145

target_mechanism: CD122-biased pegylated IL-2 pathway agonist + anti-PD-1
outcome: Phase 3 negative: bempeg + nivolumab did not improve ORR, PFS, or OS vs nivolumab alone in first-line melanoma; program discontinued.
resistance_mechanism: IL-2-pathway agonism did not add non-redundant benefit to PD-1 blockade; expanded peripheral T cells were a pharmacodynamic correlate that did not convert to intratumoral efficacy.
citation: Diab A et al. (PIVOT IO-001) J Clin Oncol 2023. PMID (verify - unresolved)

cancer_type: Untreated metastatic/PD-L1-selected non-small cell lung cancer (first-line)
outcome: Phase 3 negative: durvalumab (or durvalumab+tremelimumab) did not significantly improve OS vs chemotherapy in the PD-L1 >=25% primary population.
resistance_mechanism: PD-L1 >=25% cutoff and blood-TMB exploratory selection failed to identify the benefiting population; the chosen biomarker threshold diluted any true responder signal.
citation: Rizvi NA et al. JAMA Oncol 2020;6:661-674. PMID 32271377

outcome: Phase 3 negative: pembrolizumab + chemotherapy did not significantly improve PFS or OS vs chemotherapy alone; hierarchical testing halted.
resistance_mechanism: Adding PD-1 blockade to chemotherapy without biomarker enrichment provided no additive benefit; antagonism/timing and unselected population diluted effect.
citation: Powles T et al. Lancet Oncol 2021;22:931-945. PMID 34051178

target_mechanism: Anti-PD-L1 blockade + MEK inhibition (intended to increase MHC-I/T-cell infiltration)
outcome: Phase 3 negative: atezolizumab + cobimetinib did not improve OS vs regorafenib in chemorefractory MSS mCRC (HR 1.00).
resistance_mechanism: MEK inhibition did not convert cold MSS CRC to inflamed in patients; combination rationale from preclinical models failed to translate to a low-TMB, T-cell-excluded human tumor.
citation: Eng C et al. Lancet Oncol 2019;20:849-861. PMID 31003911

target_mechanism: Prime-boost whole-cell GM-CSF vaccine + live-attenuated Listeria expressing mesothelin
outcome: Phase 2b negative: CY/GVAX + CRS-207 did not improve OS vs single-agent chemotherapy or CRS-207 alone in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer.
resistance_mechanism: Vaccine-induced mesothelin-specific T cells could not penetrate the desmoplastic, myeloid-excluded pancreatic TME; no meaningful anti-tumor activity.
citation: Le DT et al. (ECLIPSE) Clin Cancer Res 2019. PMID (verify - unresolved)

target_mechanism: Chimeric antigen receptor T cells against EGFRvIII neoantigen
outcome: No objective clinical benefit despite CAR-T trafficking to tumor; antigen decreased in most post-infusion tumors.
resistance_mechanism: Antigen escape (loss/decrease of EGFRvIII after CAR-T pressure) plus adaptive immunosuppression in the TME (upregulated IDO1, PD-L1, Treg/myeloid infiltration).
citation: O'Rourke DM et al. Sci Transl Med 2017;9:eaaa0984. PMID 28724573

drug: Autologous anti-HER2 (trastuzumab-based scFv) third-generation CAR-T cells
outcome: Fatal outcome: rapid cytokine release and pulmonary toxicity, death within days of a single high-dose CAR-T infusion.
resistance_mechanism: On-target/off-tumor toxicity: low-level HER2 on normal lung epithelium recognized by high-avidity CAR-T, triggering lethal cytokine storm rather than tumor resistance per se.
citation: Morgan RA et al. Mol Ther 2010;18:843-851. PMID 20179677

cancer_type: Metastatic melanoma and myeloma (MAGE-A3-directed TCR therapy)
drug: Affinity-enhanced MAGE-A3 (a3a) TCR-engineered autologous T cells
target_mechanism: HLA-A*01-restricted TCR-transduced T cells against MAGE-A3
outcome: Two fatal cardiac events: patients died of cardiogenic shock/myocardial damage days after infusion.
resistance_mechanism: On-target/off-tumor cross-reactivity: affinity-enhanced TCR recognized an unrelated titin-derived peptide in cardiac muscle, causing lethal myocardial T-cell attack.
citation: Linette GP et al. Blood 2013;122:863-871. PMID 23770775; Cameron BJ et al. Sci Transl Med 2013;5:197ra103. PMID 23926201

cancer_type: Metastatic melanoma / synovial sarcoma / esophageal (MAGE-A3 TCR, HLA-A*02)
outcome: Severe neurotoxicity with two deaths from progressive necrotizing leukoencephalopathy after MAGE-A3 TCR T cells.
resistance_mechanism: On-target/off-tumor toxicity: unexpected MAGE-A12 expression in human brain recognized by the TCR, causing fatal CNS inflammation.
citation: Morgan RA et al. J Immunother 2013;36:133-151. PMID 23377668

outcome: Relapse after initial response driven by tumor genomic evolution; identified JAK1/JAK2 loss-of-function and B2M truncating mutations in resistant tumors.
resistance_mechanism: JAK1/2 loss-of-function abolishes IFN-gamma sensitivity (no PD-L1 induction, no growth arrest); B2M loss ablates surface MHC-I -> combined interferon-insensitivity and antigen-presentation loss.
citation: Zaretsky JM et al. N Engl J Med 2016;375:819-829. PMID 27433843

outcome: Non-responding tumors harbored baseline JAK1/JAK2 loss-of-function mutations conferring innate anti-PD-1 resistance.
resistance_mechanism: Genetic disruption of the IFN-gamma-JAK-STAT signaling axis renders tumor cells insensitive to interferon-mediated antiproliferative and antigen-presentation effects of reinvigorated T cells.
citation: Shin DS et al. Cancer Discov 2017;7:188-201. PMID 27903500

outcome: Non-responders enriched for genomic defects in interferon-gamma pathway genes (IFNGR1/2, JAK2, IRF1) and copy-number loss of IFN-gamma pathway components.
resistance_mechanism: Loss of interferon-gamma receptor/downstream signaling impairs tumor response to T-cell-derived IFN-gamma, blunting the antiproliferative and antigen-presentation effects required for checkpoint efficacy.

outcome: Loss of beta-2-microglobulin (B2M) associated with resistance and poor survival on checkpoint therapy.
resistance_mechanism: B2M loss (biallelic mutation/deletion) eliminates surface MHC-I assembly, so tumor cells cannot present antigen to CD8 T cells -> antigen-presentation escape.
citation: Sade-Feldman M et al. Nat Commun 2017;8:1136. PMID 29070816

cancer_type: Non-small cell lung cancer / multi-tumor (immune escape via HLA loss)
target_mechanism: MHC class I allele-specific loss of heterozygosity
outcome: HLA LOH is a common, subclonal immune-escape mechanism enabling retention of unpresented neoantigens under immune pressure.
resistance_mechanism: Allele-specific HLA loss reduces the neoantigen repertoire presentable to T cells, allowing immune evasion even with intact total MHC-I and high mutational burden.
citation: McGranahan N et al. Cell 2017;171:1259-1271. PMID 29107330

cancer_type: Non-small cell lung cancer (acquired resistance to anti-PD-1)
outcome: Relapse after response associated with elimination of 7-18 mutation-associated neoantigens in resistant tumors.
resistance_mechanism: Immunoediting: T-cell pressure selects for outgrowth of tumor subclones that have lost immunogenic neoantigens (via deletion or altered transcription), collapsing the target repertoire.
citation: Anagnostou V et al. Cancer Discov 2017;7:264-276. PMID 28031159

outcome: Tumor-intrinsic active WNT/beta-catenin signaling correlated with absence of intratumoral T cells and resistance to checkpoint blockade in melanoma models and patient samples.
resistance_mechanism: Beta-catenin activation suppresses CCL4/BATF3 dendritic-cell recruitment, preventing T-cell priming and infiltration -> non-inflamed 'cold' tumor unresponsive to checkpoint therapy.
citation: Spranger S et al. Nature 2015;523:231-235. PMID 25970248

outcome: PTEN loss in melanoma associated with reduced T-cell infiltration and inferior outcomes with anti-PD-1 therapy.
resistance_mechanism: PTEN loss/PI3K-AKT activation increases immunosuppressive cytokines (VEGF) and autophagy, decreasing T-cell trafficking and killing -> TME-mediated immune exclusion.
citation: Peng W et al. Cancer Discov 2016;6:202-216. PMID 26645196

target_mechanism: Checkpoint blockade with compensatory inhibitory-receptor upregulation
outcome: Tumors escaping anti-PD-1 upregulated the alternative checkpoint TIM-3 on T cells; adding TIM-3 blockade restored responses in models.
resistance_mechanism: Feedback reactivation of immunosuppression: compensatory upregulation of alternative inhibitory receptors (TIM-3, later LAG-3) on exhausted T cells re-establishes suppression after PD-1 blockade.
citation: Koyama S et al. Nat Commun 2016;7:10501. PMID 26883990

target_mechanism: Checkpoint blockade opposed by MDSC/TAM immunosuppression
outcome: High intratumoral myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC) burden limited anti-PD-1 efficacy; CXCR2 blockade to deplete MDSCs restored checkpoint response in models.
resistance_mechanism: MDSC/tumor-associated-macrophage infiltration suppresses effector T cells (arginase, iNOS, TGF-beta, PD-L1), producing a suppressive TME that blunts checkpoint blockade independent of tumor-cell genetics.
citation: Highfill SL et al. Sci Transl Med 2014;6:237ra67. PMID 24848257

target_mechanism: Bioreductive hypoxic-cell cytotoxin activated under low pO2; targets radioresistant hypoxic fraction
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: no improvement in OS, failure-free survival, or locoregional control vs cisplatin-RT (n~861)
resistance_mechanism: Hypoxia targeting insufficient; heterogeneous/dynamic hypoxia not captured, no hypoxia-biomarker selection
citation: Rischin D et al. J Clin Oncol 2010;28:2989-2995, PMID 20479425

outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: no OS/PFS improvement; closed early for futility
resistance_mechanism: Hypoxic-fraction targeting did not translate to outcome benefit; no hypoxia imaging/biomarker selection
citation: DiSilvestro PA et al. J Clin Oncol 2014;32:458-464, PMID 24395863

target_mechanism: Allosteric hemoglobin modifier lowering O2 affinity to increase tumor oxygenation/radiosensitivity
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: failed primary OS in all-comers; breast subgroup signal not reproduced in ENRICH; not approved
resistance_mechanism: Reoxygenation insufficient; subgroup benefit not reproducible; hypoxia not the dominant radioresistance driver in most brain mets
citation: Suh JH et al. J Clin Oncol 2006;24:106-114, PMID 16314623

target_mechanism: Redox-active texaphyrin radiosensitizer generating ROS / depleting reducing equivalents
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: no significant survival difference (5.2 vs 4.9 mo); NSCLC-subset signal did not yield approval
resistance_mechanism: ROS-based radiosensitization did not overcome intrinsic radioresistance/repair; unselected population, no predictive biomarker
citation: Mehta MP et al. J Clin Oncol 2003;21:2529-2536, PMID 12829672

target_mechanism: Cyclic RGD inhibitor of integrins alphaVbeta3/alphaVbeta5; anti-angiogenic putative radiosensitizer
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: no OS/PFS benefit (median OS 26.3 vs 26.3 mo) despite MGMT enrichment; discontinued
resistance_mechanism: Integrin alphaVbeta3/5 blockade bypassed by redundant integrins and parallel adhesion/angiogenic pathways
citation: Stupp R et al. Lancet Oncol 2014;15:1100-1108, PMID 25163906

outcome: NEGATIVE randomized Phase 2: no biological activity by primary endpoint; ended cilengitide development with CENTRIC
resistance_mechanism: Redundant integrin/adhesion signaling; integrin blockade not a driver-level vulnerability
citation: Nabors LB et al. Neuro Oncol 2015;17:708-717, PMID 25762461

target_mechanism: Anti-VEGF-A monoclonal antibody; vascular normalization hypothesized to improve radiosensitivity
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: no OS benefit; PFS gain non-significant; more symptom/neurocognitive decline
resistance_mechanism: VEGF blockade evasion via alternative pro-angiogenic factors (FGF, Ang-2, PlGF) and vessel co-option; pseudoresponse
citation: Gilbert MR et al. N Engl J Med 2014;370:699-708, PMID 24552317

outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: no OS benefit (16.8 vs 16.7 mo); PFS improved but OS unchanged, confirming RTOG 0825
resistance_mechanism: Compensatory angiogenic bypass; anti-VEGF pseudoresponse; anti-angiogenesis does not durably reverse GBM radioresistance
citation: Chinot OL et al. N Engl J Med 2014;370:709-722, PMID 24552318

target_mechanism: Anti-EGFR mAb used as a 'less-toxic' radiosensitizer substitute for cisplatin
outcome: NEGATIVE de-escalation Phase 3: cetuximab-RT INFERIOR to cisplatin-RT for OS and locoregional control; no toxicity reduction
resistance_mechanism: EGFR inhibition a weaker radiosensitizer than cisplatin in HPV+ disease; EGFR not the dominant survival driver
citation: Gillison ML et al. Lancet 2019;393:40-50, PMID 30449625

outcome: NEGATIVE de-escalation Phase 3: more recurrences and worse 2-yr OS with cetuximab-RT; confirms RTOG 1016
resistance_mechanism: Inferior radiosensitization vs platinum; EGFR blockade does not replace cisplatin-RT DNA-crosslink synergy
citation: Mehanna H et al. Lancet 2019;393:51-60, PMID 30449623

drug: Cetuximab added to cisplatin + accelerated RT
target_mechanism: Anti-EGFR mAb added on top of standard chemoRT (intensification)
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: adding cetuximab did NOT improve PFS or OS; increased mucositis/skin toxicity
resistance_mechanism: Redundant EGFR downstream signaling (RAS/PI3K) already engaged; on-mechanism toxicity without efficacy gain
citation: Ang KK et al. J Clin Oncol 2014;32:2940-2950, PMID 25154822

drug: Dose-escalated RT (74 Gy vs 60 Gy) +/- cetuximab + carbo/paclitaxel
target_mechanism: RT dose escalation; cetuximab anti-EGFR radiosensitizer
outcome: NEGATIVE/HARMFUL Phase 3: high-dose RT WORSE OS than 60 Gy (20.3 vs 28.7 mo); cetuximab no benefit
resistance_mechanism: Dose escalation increased heart/lung dose (cardiac toxicity) outweighing tumor control; EGFR blockade redundant
citation: Bradley JD et al. Lancet Oncol 2015;16:187-199, PMID 25601342

target_mechanism: RT dose escalation to improve biochemical/local control
outcome: NEGATIVE for survival: improved biochemical control but NO OS improvement; more late GI/GU toxicity
resistance_mechanism: Surrogate (biochemical control) improved without OS gain; competing risks and indolent biology dilute survival signal
citation: Michalski JM et al. JAMA Oncol 2018;4:e180039, PMID 29543933

cancer_type: Head and neck SCC (locally advanced, unresected)
target_mechanism: Oral SMAC mimetic / IAP (cIAP1, XIAP) antagonist; promotes apoptosis and radiosensitization
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: no improvement in event-free survival; terminated June 2024; contradicts positive Phase 2
resistance_mechanism: Forcing apoptotic vs immunogenic cell death may blunt chemoRT immune activation; Phase 2 signal not reproducible at scale
citation: Bourhis J et al. J Clin Oncol 2025; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04459715

target_mechanism: PKC-beta / PI3K-AKT pathway inhibitor; explored as radio/chemo-potentiator
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: not superior to lomustine for PFS or OS; glioma development halted
resistance_mechanism: PKC-beta not a non-redundant driver; parallel PI3K/MAPK signaling maintains proliferation and radioresistance
citation: Wick W et al. J Clin Oncol 2010;28:1168-1174, PMID 20124186

target_mechanism: Sequential intensification: upfront cytoreduction + micrometastasis control before definitive chemoRT
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: adding induction chemo before chemoRT did NOT improve OS; more toxicity
resistance_mechanism: Induction intensification adds toxicity/delay without improving the RT-controlled locoregional compartment
citation: Haddad R et al. Lancet Oncol 2013;14:257-264, PMID 23474112

cancer_type: Head and neck SCC (locally advanced, N2/N3)
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: no significant OS benefit from induction chemo added to chemoRT
resistance_mechanism: No additive mechanism over definitive chemoRT; added systemic toxicity
citation: Cohen EEW et al. J Clin Oncol 2014;32:2735-2743, PMID 25049329

drug: Prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI) vs MRI surveillance
target_mechanism: Prophylactic whole-brain RT to sterilize subclinical brain micrometastases
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: with MRI surveillance, PCI did NOT improve OS (11.6 vs 13.7 mo); reduced brain-mets only
resistance_mechanism: PCI controls a surrogate (CNS relapse) without altering systemic disease-driven mortality; MRI salvage negates advantage
citation: Takahashi T et al. Lancet Oncol 2017;18:663-671, PMID 28343976

target_mechanism: Fully human anti-EGFR mAb as radiosensitizer / cisplatin adjunct or substitute
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 2: panitumumab + chemoRT no locoregional benefit; panitumumab-RT without cisplatin INFERIOR
resistance_mechanism: EGFR blockade cannot replace platinum radiosensitization; redundant downstream signaling
citation: Mesia R et al. Lancet Oncol 2015;16:208-220, PMID 25596660

target_mechanism: Humanized anti-EGFR mAb (intermediate affinity) as radiosensitizer
outcome: NEGATIVE / no meaningful benefit; no durable responses or survival benefit in DIPG; not adopted
resistance_mechanism: EGFR not the driver in H3K27M-driven DIPG; antibody radiosensitization ineffective against intrinsic radioresistance
citation: Bartels U et al. J Neurooncol 2014;120:341-347, PMID 25073688

cancer_type: Head and neck SCC (hypoxic modification, regionally positive context)
drug: Nimorazole + primary RT (hypoxic radiosensitizer) - context entry
target_mechanism: Nitroimidazole hypoxic-cell radiosensitizer (electron-affinic, mimics oxygen in fixing DNA radical damage)
sponsor: Danish Head and Neck Cancer Group
outcome: MIXED/CONTEXT: POSITIVE in DAHANCA 5 but NOT reproduced or adopted outside Scandinavia; near-unique success among hypoxic sensitizers
resistance_mechanism: Hypoxic radiosensitization benefit is population/biomarker-dependent (HPV-negative, hypoxia-high); generalization fails without hypoxia-signature selection
citation: Overgaard J et al. Radiother Oncol 1998;46:135-146, PMID 9510041

cancer_type: Head and neck SCC / multiple solid tumors (historical hypoxic sensitizer)
outcome: NEGATIVE: repeated large Phase 3 trials showed no consistent survival/local-control benefit; dose-limiting neuropathy; abandoned
resistance_mechanism: Neurotoxicity capped achievable drug concentration below radiosensitizing threshold (on-mechanism toxicity); unselected patients
citation: Overgaard J. J Clin Oncol 2007;25:4066-4074 (meta-analysis), PMID 17827455

outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: no overall improvement in locoregional control or survival vs RT alone
resistance_mechanism: Hypoxia modification insufficient without patient selection; reoxygenation during fractionation dilutes benefit
citation: Lee DJ et al. Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys 1995;32:567-576, PMID 7790243

target_mechanism: Hypoxia stabilizes HIF-1alpha; reduced O2-dependent fixation of RT-induced DNA radical damage (oxygen enhancement ratio ~2.5-3x)
outcome: Established mechanism: hypoxic regions 2-3x more radioresistant; underlies repeated failure of hypoxia-modifier trials lacking biomarker selection
resistance_mechanism: Low pO2 prevents oxygen fixation of DNA damage; HIF-1alpha program promotes survival, stemness, reoxygenation-driven repopulation
citation: Brown JM, Wilson WR. Nat Rev Cancer 2004;4:437-447, PMID 15170446

target_mechanism: CD133+ glioma stem cells preferentially activate DNA-damage checkpoint (CHK1/CHK2) and survive RT, repopulating tumor
outcome: Established mechanism: CD133+ fraction enriched after irradiation and drives recurrence; local failure despite bulk cytoreduction
resistance_mechanism: Stem-cell subpopulation with enhanced checkpoint/DNA-repair survives and repopulates (bulk 'response' masks resistant reservoir)
citation: Bao S et al. Nature 2006;444:756-760, PMID 17051156

target_mechanism: Upregulated NHEJ (DNA-PKcs) and homologous recombination (ATM, RAD51, BRCA) rapidly repair RT-induced double-strand breaks
outcome: Established mechanism; rationale for DNA-PK/ATM inhibitor + RT combinations; high repair capacity predicts radioresistance
resistance_mechanism: Efficient DSB repair removes the lethal lesions RT depends on; DNA-PKcs/ATM hyperactivation correlates with clinical radioresistance
citation: Goldstein M, Kastan MB. Annu Rev Med 2015;66:129-143, PMID 25423595

target_mechanism: Surviving clonogens accelerate proliferation after ~day 21-28 of fractionated RT, requiring escalating dose to counter regrowth
outcome: Established mechanism: prolonged/interrupted RT courses lose control; basis for accelerated fractionation
resistance_mechanism: Repopulation of clonogenic tumor cells during protracted fractionation outpaces cell kill (temporal escape)
citation: Withers HR, Taylor JM, Maciejewski B. Acta Oncol 1988;27:131-146, PMID 3390344

drug: N/A - radioresistance mechanism (cell-cycle checkpoint adaptation, CHK1/WEE1)
target_mechanism: RT-activated ATR-CHK1 and WEE1 arrest cells at G2/M, allowing DNA repair before mitosis
outcome: Established mechanism; rationale for WEE1/CHK1 inhibitor radiosensitizers; robust checkpoint = radioresistance in TP53-mutant tumors
resistance_mechanism: G2/M checkpoint delay allows repair of RT damage; TP53 loss shifts reliance to G2 checkpoint, enabling survival despite unrepaired damage
citation: Morgan MA, Lawrence TS. Clin Cancer Res 2015;21:2898-2904, PMID 26133775

cancer_type: Head and neck SCC (EGFR-inhibitor radioresistance mechanism)
drug: N/A - resistance mechanism to cetuximab/EGFR-inhibitor + RT
target_mechanism: EGFR blockade bypassed by nuclear EGFR (DNA-PK activation), HER3/MET/AXL activation, and RAS/PI3K signaling
outcome: Mechanistic basis for cetuximab-RT/panitumumab-RT clinical failures (RTOG 0522, RTOG 1016, De-ESCALaTE, CONCERT)
resistance_mechanism: Nuclear EGFR translocation activates DNA-PK repair; parallel RTK (MET, AXL, HER3) and RAS/PI3K bypass sustain repair despite surface-EGFR blockade
citation: Bonner JA et al. N Engl J Med 2006;354:567-578; Rodemann HP mechanism reviews, PMID 16467544

target_mechanism: Anti-cancer quinolone-derivative topoisomerase II inhibitor / DNA intercalator
outcome: Phase 3 negative: median OS 7.5 mo (vosaroxin+cytarabine) vs 6.1 mo (placebo+cytarabine), HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.73-1.02), primary OS endpoint not met; CR rate improved (30.1% vs 16.3%).
resistance_mechanism: Broadly cytotoxic DNA-damaging agent added to cytarabine with no molecularly stratified target; benefit confined to post-hoc subgroups (age >=60, censoring for transplant), consistent with an unselected R/R population diluting any true signal.
citation: Ravandi F et al. Lancet Oncol 2015;16(9):1025-36. PMID 26234174

target_mechanism: Anti-CD33 antibody-drug conjugate delivering a pyrrolobenzodiazepine (PBD) DNA-crosslinking dimer
outcome: Phase 3 halted June 2017 by the IDMC: excess deaths (including fatal infections) in the vadastuximab-talirine + HMA arm vs HMA alone; entire program suspended.
resistance_mechanism: On-mechanism ADC/PBD toxicity — CD33 is expressed on normal myeloid progenitors, so target-mediated marrow suppression plus DNA-crosslink toxicity drove fatal infections rather than an efficacy failure.
citation: Seattle Genetics announcement; ASH Clinical News 2017; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02785900 (PMID (verify - unresolved))

target_mechanism: Ras-mimetic / RAS-RAF-PI3K pathway and PLK1 signaling inhibitor (styryl benzyl sulfone)
outcome: Phase 3 negative: median OS 8.2 mo (IV rigosertib+BSC) vs 5.8 mo (BSC), HR 0.87, p=0.33; primary OS endpoint not met. Post-hoc primary-HMA-failure subgroup showed OS benefit.
resistance_mechanism: Diffuse multi-kinase/Ras-mimetic mechanism without a validated predictive biomarker; any activity concentrated in an unplanned subgroup, indicating the target relationship was correlative rather than a stratified driver.
citation: Garcia-Manero G et al. Lancet Oncol 2016;17(4):496-508. PMID 26968357

target_mechanism: Ras-mimetic / RAS-RAF-PI3K and PLK signaling inhibitor
outcome: Second confirmatory Phase 3 (rigosertib vs physician's choice) in HR-MDS after HMA failure; did not meet the primary OS endpoint, echoing ONTIME.
resistance_mechanism: Repeated failure of the same unstratified mechanism across two Phase 3 trials; no enrichment biomarker was ever prospectively validated to identify responders.
citation: INSPIRE Phase 3 (ASH 2020 / Onconova); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02562443 (PMID (verify - unresolved))

cancer_type: AML (newly diagnosed, unfit for intensive induction)
target_mechanism: Next-generation hypomethylating agent; dinucleotide of decitabine + deoxyguanosine (DNMT inhibitor, resistant to cytidine deaminase)
outcome: Phase 3 negative: failed co-primary endpoints of CR and OS vs physician's choice (azacitidine/decitabine/LDAC) in 815 treatment-naive unfit AML patients; ASTRAL-2 and ASTRAL-3 also negative.
resistance_mechanism: Longer decitabine exposure did not overcome intrinsic HMA resistance; the same DNMT-directed mechanism as the comparator, so no differentiated pathway to beat control (mechanistic redundancy vs standard HMAs).
citation: Fenaux P et al. Lancet Haematol 2023 (ASTRAL-1); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02348489 (PMID (verify - unresolved))

outcome: Phase 3 negative: median OS 5.6 mo (volasertib+LDAC) vs 6.5 mo (placebo+LDAC), HR 0.97, p=0.76; unfavorable OS trend driven by infections/febrile neutropenia.
resistance_mechanism: Anti-mitotic PLK1 inhibition is not tumor-selective; added myelosuppression/fatal infections outweighed any leukemic-cell effect (mechanism-based toxicity in an unfit population).
citation: Doehner H et al. Blood 2021;138(2):145-158 (Adjunctive Volasertib Phase 3). PMID 34350385

target_mechanism: Oral nucleoside analog (2'-C-cyano-2'-deoxy-arabinofuranosyl-cytosine) causing single-strand DNA breaks
outcome: Phase 3 negative: sapacitabine alternating with decitabine did not improve OS vs decitabine monotherapy (482 pts); CR rate improved in some subgroups (WBC <10).
resistance_mechanism: Adding a second cytotoxic nucleoside to an HMA backbone lacked a resistance-directed rationale; overlapping cytotoxic mechanism yielded no OS gain over decitabine alone.
citation: Kantarjian HM et al. Cancer 2021;127(23):4421-4431 (SEAMLESS). PMID 34424530

target_mechanism: Lipophilic 5'-elaidic-acid ester of cytarabine designed for hENT1-independent cellular uptake
outcome: Phase 3 negative: median OS 3.5 mo (elacytarabine) vs 3.3 mo (investigator choice), HR 0.97; no difference in response or RFS (381 pts).
resistance_mechanism: Rationale was to bypass low hENT1 transporter expression (a proposed cytarabine-resistance mechanism), but hENT1-independent delivery did not translate to benefit — the transporter was a correlate, not the limiting driver of ara-C resistance.
citation: Roboz GJ et al. J Clin Oncol 2014;32(18):1919-26 (CLAVELA). PMID 24841975

target_mechanism: Third-generation pan-BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor active against T315I gatekeeper mutation
outcome: Efficacious (MCyR 60%, active vs T315I) but benefit-risk problem: cumulative arterial occlusive events ~25-31% (MI, cerebrovascular, peripheral) at 45 mg/day led to a 2013 label boxed warning and dose reduction (later OPTIC trial).
resistance_mechanism: On-mechanism vascular toxicity: potent multi-kinase (incl VEGFR) inhibition and endothelial effects cause arterial thrombosis, a class/target-linked harm rather than loss of anti-leukemic efficacy.
citation: Cortes JE et al. N Engl J Med 2013;369(19):1783-96 (PACE). PMID 24180494

target_mechanism: Sulfonylhydrazine alkylating agent (chloroethylating + carbamoylating; targets O6 of guanine)
outcome: Failed to gain approval; excess early mortality/toxicity and no OS advantage vs comparators in poor-risk elderly AML; development discontinued.
resistance_mechanism: Alkylator activity counteracted by MGMT-mediated DNA-repair of O6-alkylguanine lesions; added pulmonary/marrow toxicity in elderly patients with no offsetting survival gain.
citation: Schiller GJ et al. J Clin Oncol 2010 (laromustine elderly AML); PMID 20026800

target_mechanism: Anti-CD33 antibody-drug conjugate delivering calicheamicin (DNA double-strand breaks)
outcome: At the original 9 mg/m2 dose, S0106 showed no benefit and higher fatal induction toxicity, prompting voluntary US withdrawal in 2010; later reinstated in 2017 at fractionated 3 mg/m2 dosing (ALFA-0701) — a benefit-risk/dosing case, not a target failure.
resistance_mechanism: Original failure was dose/schedule-driven hepatotoxicity (veno-occlusive disease) and early mortality (mechanism-based toxicity); efficacy re-emerged once dosing was optimized. Intrinsic resistance also linked to P-glycoprotein/MDR1 efflux of calicheamicin.
citation: Petersdorf SH et al. Blood 2013;121(24):4854-60 (S0106). PMID 23321251

target_mechanism: First-generation multi-targeted FLT3 tyrosine kinase inhibitor
outcome: Phase 3 negative: adding lestaurtinib to salvage chemotherapy did not improve CR or OS; correlative analysis showed most patients did not achieve sustained FLT3 inhibition in plasma.
resistance_mechanism: Inadequate/inconsistent target inhibition (high plasma protein binding, alpha-1-acid glycoprotein sequestration) meant FLT3 was rarely fully suppressed in vivo — pharmacologic failure to engage the driver.

target_mechanism: HSP90 chaperone inhibitor (destabilizes client oncoproteins incl FLT3, KIT)
outcome: Did not advance in AML; limited single-agent activity and no differentiated benefit in combination; broader ganetespib program (e.g., NSCLC GALAXY-2) also failed.
resistance_mechanism: HSP90 blockade triggers compensatory heat-shock response (HSF1/HSP70 induction) that re-stabilizes clients; broad chaperone targeting lacked a stratified oncogenic-addiction rationale in AML.
citation: Ganetespib (STA-9090) early-phase AML program (Synta Pharmaceuticals); no pivotal Phase-3 publication - program-level entry, exact NCT/PMID not established

target_mechanism: Second-generation purine nucleoside analog (ribonucleotide reductase + DNA polymerase inhibition)
outcome: Phase 3: clofarabine + LDAC improved response/EFS but did NOT improve OS vs LDAC alone in older AML; more toxicity offset early benefit.
resistance_mechanism: Higher remission rates did not convert to survival because added myelotoxicity/early mortality (and relapse) negated the response advantage — response was a surrogate that did not track OS.
citation: Faderl S et al. Blood 2012;120(23):4534-6 (CLASSIC I); PMID (verify - unresolved)

target_mechanism: Farnesyltransferase inhibitor (blocks prenylation of RAS and other CAAX proteins)
outcome: Phase 3 negative: tipifarnib did not improve OS vs best supportive care in older newly diagnosed AML; no validated predictive biomarker at the time.
resistance_mechanism: FTI blockade is bypassed by alternative geranylgeranylation of K-RAS/N-RAS, and the drug was given to a molecularly unselected population (later work pointed to CXCL12/other biomarkers), so the intended RAS-pathway dependency was not present in most patients.
citation: Harousseau JL et al. Blood 2009;114(6):1166-73. PMID 19168783

target_mechanism: NEDD8-activating enzyme (NAE) inhibitor; blocks cullin-RING ligase neddylation
outcome: Phase 3 negative: pevonedistat + azacitidine did not significantly improve event-free survival or OS vs azacitidine alone in HR-MDS/CMML/low-blast AML.
resistance_mechanism: Adding NAE inhibition to an HMA lacked a biomarker-defined dependency; the two agents did not synergize on a shared, validated resistance node in the trial population.
citation: Sekeres MA et al. (PANTHER Phase 3, 2023); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03268954 (PMID (verify - unresolved))

target_mechanism: Anti-CD47 macrophage-checkpoint ("don't-eat-me") antibody enabling phagocytosis of leukemic cells
outcome: Phase 3 program halted 2023-2024: ENHANCE (HR-MDS + azacitidine) stopped for futility; AML studies stopped for futility/potential harm (increased deaths); AML/MDS development discontinued.
resistance_mechanism: Innate immune checkpoint blockade did not overcome the immunosuppressive AML/MDS microenvironment; on-target anemia (CD47 on RBCs) and lack of adaptive anti-leukemic response limited efficacy.
citation: Gilead Sciences press releases 2023-2024; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04313881 (ENHANCE)

target_mechanism: E-selectin antagonist; disrupts leukemia-stem-cell adhesion to bone-marrow vascular niche to overcome microenvironment-mediated chemoresistance
outcome: Phase 3 negative top-line (2024): adding uproleselan to salvage chemotherapy did not significantly improve overall survival vs chemotherapy alone in R/R AML.
resistance_mechanism: The E-selectin/niche-adhesion axis, though a real chemoresistance mechanism preclinically, was not the rate-limiting driver of survival in the biomarker-unselected trial population.
citation: GlycoMimetics Phase 3 top-line 2024; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03616470 (PMID (verify - unresolved))

outcome: Phase 3 discontinued in 2020 after an interim futility analysis: pracinostat + azacitidine unlikely to meet the primary OS endpoint vs azacitidine alone.
resistance_mechanism: Broad epigenetic HDAC inhibition added to an HMA without a predictive biomarker; overlapping/undirected epigenetic mechanism plus added toxicity yielded no survival gain.
citation: Helsinn/MEI Pharma announcement 2020; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03151408 (PMID (verify - unresolved))

target_mechanism: Type II (DFG-out) FLT3-ITD selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor
outcome: On-target acquired resistance: relapses driven by secondary FLT3 tyrosine-kinase-domain (TKD) mutations, especially the D835/Y842 activation-loop and F691L gatekeeper mutations, which abolish type-II inhibitor binding.
resistance_mechanism: Secondary FLT3-TKD point mutations (D835, F691L gatekeeper) restore kinase activity in the ITD-mutant clone despite continued drug (classic on-mechanism target-mutation escape).
citation: Smith CC et al. Nature 2012;485(7397):260-3. PMID 22504184

target_mechanism: Type I FLT3 tyrosine kinase inhibitor (active against both ITD and TKD/D835)
outcome: Effective (approved), but acquired resistance emerges via activation of RAS/MAPK bypass signaling (NRAS/KRAS, PTPN11, CBL mutations) and, less often, secondary FLT3-F691L; some relapses show FLT3-independent survival.
resistance_mechanism: Bypass/parallel-pathway reactivation: outgrowth of RAS-MAPK-mutant subclones sustains proliferation independent of FLT3 inhibition, plus on-target F691L gatekeeper mutation.
citation: McMahon CM et al. Cancer Discov 2019;9(8):1050-1063. PMID 31048320

target_mechanism: Multi-kinase inhibitor with FLT3-ITD activity (type II)
outcome: Responses in FLT3-ITD AML are typically transient; relapse driven by secondary FLT3-TKD mutations (D835, F691L) and RAS/parallel-pathway activation.
resistance_mechanism: Acquired FLT3 activation-loop/gatekeeper (D835, F691L) mutations plus RAS-pathway bypass; also microenvironment/FLT3-ligand surges blunt type-II inhibitor efficacy.
citation: Man CH et al. Blood 2012;119(22):5133-43 (sorafenib FLT3-ITD resistance); PMID 22368270

outcome: Overall a landmark success, but resistance/relapse driven by BCR-ABL1 kinase-domain point mutations — most critically the T315I gatekeeper mutation, which confers resistance to imatinib and all early TKIs.
resistance_mechanism: Secondary BCR-ABL1 kinase-domain mutations (>100 described; T315I gatekeeper, P-loop mutations) sterically block or reduce TKI binding while preserving oncogenic kinase activity.
citation: Gorre ME et al. Science 2001;293(5531):876-80. PMID 11423618

outcome: More potent than imatinib but each has a mutation-specific resistance profile (e.g., F317L/V299L for dasatinib; Y253H/E255K/F359 for nilotinib) and NONE covers T315I; compound mutations cause pan-TKI resistance.
resistance_mechanism: Selection of mutation-specific BCR-ABL1 kinase-domain variants and stepwise compound mutations under sequential TKI pressure; T315I gatekeeper remains uncovered until ponatinib/asciminib.
citation: Soverini S et al. Blood 2011;118(5):1208-15 (BCR-ABL1 KD mutations); PMID 21562040

target_mechanism: Mutant IDH1 (R132) inhibitor; blocks oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate to restore myeloid differentiation
outcome: Acquired resistance via IDH isoform switching (emergence of IDH2 mutations restoring 2-HG), second-site IDH1 mutations, and RTK/RAS-pathway co-mutations.
resistance_mechanism: Isoform switching (IDH1->IDH2) and second-site mutations at the drug-binding dimer interface restore 2-HG production; parallel receptor-tyrosine-kinase/RAS mutations provide differentiation-independent survival.
citation: Intlekofer AM et al. Nature 2018;559:125-129 (acquired resistance via IDH2 dimer-interface mutations), PMID 29950729

target_mechanism: Mutant IDH2 (R140/R172) inhibitor; lowers 2-hydroxyglutarate to induce differentiation
outcome: Acquired resistance via IDH isoform switching (emergent IDH1 mutations) and second-site IDH2 mutations (e.g., Q316E, I319M) that disrupt inhibitor binding while restoring 2-HG.
resistance_mechanism: Isoform switching (IDH2->IDH1) and trans/second-site IDH2 mutations at the dimer interface re-elevate 2-HG; differentiation block re-established despite on-target drug.
citation: Intlekofer AM et al. Nature 2018;559:125-129 (acquired resistance via IDH2 dimer-interface mutations), PMID 29950729

outcome: Phase 3 negative: enasidenib did not significantly improve OS vs conventional care regimens in older R/R IDH2-mutant AML (missed primary endpoint), despite CR/differentiation activity.
resistance_mechanism: Single-agent differentiation therapy in heavily pretreated, clonally heterogeneous R/R AML: co-occurring RAS/RTK and other mutations drive IDH2-independent survival, so on-target 2-HG lowering did not extend OS.
citation: de Botton S et al. Blood 2023 (IDHENTIFY); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02577406 (PMID (verify - unresolved))

outcome: Acquired resistance via BCL2 mutations (e.g., G101V, D103) that reduce venetoclax binding, and via BAX/apoptotic-machinery loss-of-function mutations blunting mitochondrial priming.
resistance_mechanism: On-target BCL2 mutations decrease drug affinity; BAX inactivation prevents mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization, evading BH3-mimetic-induced apoptosis.
citation: Blombery P et al. Cancer Discov 2019;9(3):342-353 (BCL2 G101V); PMID 30514704

outcome: Resistance via upregulation/dependence on alternative anti-apoptotic proteins MCL1 and BCL-XL, which sequester pro-apoptotic BH3 proteins that venetoclax cannot antagonize.
resistance_mechanism: Anti-apoptotic redundancy: MCL1 (and BCL-XL) upregulation, often driven by metabolic/OXPHOS shifts and monocytic biology, provides a parallel survival pathway bypassing BCL2 inhibition.
citation: Ramsey HE et al. Cancer Discov 2018;8(12):1566-1581 (MCL1 in venetoclax resistance); PMID (verify - unresolved)

outcome: Relapse driven by outgrowth of monocytic AML subclones that are intrinsically MCL1-dependent and BCL2-low, conferring primary/acquired venetoclax resistance.
resistance_mechanism: Lineage plasticity / differentiation state: monocytic (CD14+) leukemic cells lose BCL2 dependence and rely on MCL1, so venetoclax selects for or drives a resistant monocytic phenotype.
citation: Pei S et al. Cancer Discov 2020;10(4):536-551 (monocytic venetoclax resistance). PMID 31974170

target_mechanism: Hypomethylating agents; cytidine-analog DNMT1 inhibitors (depletion of DNA methyltransferase)
outcome: Nearly all responders eventually fail HMAs; post-HMA-failure MDS has dismal (<6 mo) survival. No single recurrent mutation reliably predicts response; resistance is largely non-genetic/metabolic.
resistance_mechanism: Pharmacologic/metabolic: reduced drug activation and incorporation via low deoxycytidine kinase (DCK)/UCK, reduced nucleoside transporter (hENT1) uptake, and quiescent stem cells that escape S-phase-dependent DNMT depletion.
citation: Stomper J et al. Leukemia 2021 (HMA resistance mechanisms review); Qin T et al. Blood 2009 (DCK); PMID (verify - unresolved)

outcome: Symptom/spleen benefit but not curative; loss of response ('persistence') without clearing the JAK2 mutation, via heterodimeric reactivation of JAK-STAT signaling.
resistance_mechanism: Feedback reactivation: JAK2 transactivation through heterodimerization with JAK1/TYK2 restores STAT signaling despite continued inhibitor (type-I inhibitor persistence), rather than a JAK2 gatekeeper mutation.
citation: Koppikar P et al. Nature 2012;489(7414):155-9. PMID 22820254

target_mechanism: Second-generation dual SRC/ABL BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor
outcome: Phase 3 missed its primary endpoint: complete cytogenetic response at 12 months not superior to imatinib, largely because early GI-toxicity-driven discontinuations reduced evaluable responders (deeper molecular responses did favor bosutinib).
resistance_mechanism: On-mechanism gastrointestinal toxicity (diarrhea, hepatic enzyme elevation) caused early treatment discontinuation, undermining the strict intention-to-treat endpoint — a toxicity/endpoint-definition failure, not loss of anti-leukemic potency.
citation: Cortes JE et al. J Clin Oncol 2012;30(28):3486-92 (BELA). PMID 22949154

target_mechanism: Covalent BTK inhibitor blocking chronic-active BCR / NF-kB signaling in ABC/non-GCB DLBCL
outcome: Phase 3 negative: no EFS or OS improvement vs placebo+R-CHOP in ITT non-GCB population (EFS HR 0.934); added toxicity impaired R-CHOP delivery in patients >=60; benefit only in pre-specified age <60 subset
resistance_mechanism: Non-GCB IHC is an imperfect surrogate for BCR-addicted genetic subtypes (MCD/N1); older patients could not tolerate full-dose R-CHOP so on-mechanism toxicity diluted any benefit; BTK is one of several parallel survival inputs
citation: Younes A et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:1285-1295 (PMID 30901302)

target_mechanism: Reversible 20S proteasome inhibitor intended to suppress NF-kB in ABC-DLBCL
sponsor: University of Southampton / Cancer Research UK
outcome: Phase 3 negative primary endpoint: no PFS or OS benefit at 30 months in the molecularly-guided combined cohort; a late (5-yr) signal emerged only in ABC / molecular-high-grade subsets
resistance_mechanism: NF-kB is one of several redundant survival inputs, so proteasome inhibition adds little on top of R-CHOP; GEP subgroup benefit surfaced only with long follow-up, i.e., the unselected primary population diluted the effect
citation: Davies A et al. Lancet Oncol 2019;20:649-662 (PMID 30948276)

outcome: Phase 3 negative: 1 year of adjuvant everolimus did not improve DFS (HR 0.92; P=0.276) or OS after CR to first-line R-chemo in IPI>=3 DLBCL
resistance_mechanism: mTORC1 blockade relieves S6K-IRS1 negative feedback, reactivating PI3K-AKT; mTOR activity is a correlate rather than a validated causal driver of residual DLBCL
citation: Witzig TE et al. Ann Oncol 2018;29:707-714

outcome: Phase 3 negative: no improvement in DFS, EFS, or OS as maintenance after R-CHOP CR in high-risk DLBCL (4-yr DFS 70% vs 71%)
resistance_mechanism: PKC-beta expression is a prognostic correlate, not a causal dependency in minimal residual DLBCL; single-node inhibition is bypassed by redundant BCR/survival signaling
citation: Crump M et al. J Clin Oncol 2016;34:2484-2492

target_mechanism: Cereblon-mediated degradation of IKZF1/3, downmodulating IRF4/NF-kB in ABC-DLBCL
outcome: Phase 3 negative: no PFS benefit even in molecularly-selected ABC-DLBCL (HR 0.85; P=0.29)
resistance_mechanism: Operational population dilution: mandatory NanoString subtyping delayed treatment start and enrolled lower-risk, chemo-responsive patients, leaving little margin over an effective R-CHOP backbone; the earlier E1412 signal (clinical start) was not reproduced
citation: Nowakowski GS et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:1317-1328 (PMID 33621109)

outcome: Phase 3 stopped: no PFS or OS benefit added to R-CHOP, with increased cardiotoxicity (LV dysfunction, CHF) and GI perforation
resistance_mechanism: Tumor angiogenesis is a bystander correlate in DLBCL rather than a driver; anti-VEGF added on-mechanism cardiovascular toxicity that offset any potential benefit
citation: Seymour JF et al. J Clin Oncol 2014;32:3986-3992 (PMID (verify - unresolved))

target_mechanism: Glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 mAb with enhanced ADCC/direct cell death
outcome: Phase 3 negative: G-CHOP did not improve PFS vs R-CHOP in first-line DLBCL (HR 0.92; P=0.39) with more adverse events
resistance_mechanism: Swapping to a higher-ADCC anti-CD20 is a redundant mechanism; CD20-directed killing is already saturated by rituximab, so no new pathway is engaged
citation: Vitolo U et al. J Clin Oncol 2017;35:3529-3537 (PMID 28779999)

sponsor: Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology / NCI
outcome: Phase 3 negative: DA-EPOCH-R did not improve PFS or OS vs R-CHOP in untreated DLBCL, with greater toxicity
resistance_mechanism: Dose intensification adds no new mechanism over R-CHOP for unselected DLBCL; any benefit is restricted to rare high-grade/double-hit subsets not enriched in this population
citation: Bartlett NL et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:1790-1799 (PMID 30939090)

target_mechanism: Covalent (Cys481) BTK inhibitor of B-cell receptor signaling
outcome: Highly effective but acquired resistance and progression develop over time (with Richter transformation in a subset)
resistance_mechanism: Acquired BTK C481S abolishes covalent binding (leaving only reversible inhibition); gain-of-function PLCG2 mutations (R665W, L845F, S707Y) restore BCR signaling downstream of BTK
citation: Woyach JA et al. N Engl J Med 2014;370:2286-2294 (PMID 24869598)

outcome: Durable responses but resistance emerges, with cross-resistance to ibrutinib via the shared binding cysteine
resistance_mechanism: BTK C481S/C481R and PLCG2 mutations; shared Cys481 dependence limits sequential covalent BTKi and forces switch to non-covalent inhibitors (e.g., pirtobrutinib)
citation: Woyach JA et al. resistance analyses; Sharman JP et al. ELEVATE-TN, Lancet 2020 (PMID (verify - unresolved))

trial: Front-line combination program (6 randomized trials halted by FDA, 2016)
outcome: Six randomized combination trials halted in 2016 for excess infectious deaths (7.4% vs 3.5% control); severe immune-mediated hepatotoxicity (grade>=3 transaminitis ~52%), colitis, pneumonitis, PJP/CMV; unfavorable benefit-risk front-line
resistance_mechanism: On-mechanism/off-target immune dysregulation: PI3K-delta blockade impairs regulatory T-cell function, driving autoimmune hepatitis/colitis and opportunistic infection; toxicity, not lack of efficacy, drove failure
citation: Lampson BL et al. Blood 2016;128:195-203 (PMID 27247136)

outcome: High response rates but progression with acquired resistance on continuous or relapsed therapy
resistance_mechanism: Acquired BCL2 G101V (and D103Y, A113G, others) reduces venetoclax binding ~180-fold; parallel upregulation of MCL1/BCL-XL provides an apoptotic bypass
citation: Blombery P et al. Cancer Discov 2019;9:342-353 (PMID 30514704)

outcome: Randomized negative: adding anti-CD23 to FCR did not improve response rate or PFS in relapsed CLL; program discontinued
resistance_mechanism: CD23 is an activation-marker correlate, not a survival driver in CLL; the antibody added no independent cytotoxic mechanism beyond rituximab-based FCR
citation: Awan FT et al. Leuk Lymphoma 2014 (LUCID/152CL201), PMID 25130401; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00391066

target_mechanism: CD19 x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE)
outcome: Superior to chemotherapy but ~10-30% of relapses occur as CD19-negative disease
resistance_mechanism: CD19 antigen escape: exon-2 alternative splicing, frameshift/missense CD19 mutations and loss of surface CD19; also CD19-negative myeloid lineage switch
citation: Kantarjian H et al. N Engl J Med 2017;376:836-847 (TOWER, PMID 28249141)

outcome: High initial CR (~81%) but ~40-50% relapse, frequently with CD19-negative disease
resistance_mechanism: CD19 antigen escape via alternatively spliced/mutated CD19 (loss of the FMC63 epitope, exon-2 skipping) and lineage switch; also loss of CAR-T persistence
citation: Sotillo E et al. Cancer Discov 2015;5:1282-1295 (PMID 26516035); Maude SL et al. N Engl J Med 2018 (ELIANA)

outcome: Durable responses in ~40% but the majority relapse; roughly one-third of relapses are CD19-low/negative
resistance_mechanism: CD19 antigen loss/downregulation; immune exclusion via impaired antigen presentation and T-cell exhaustion; poor CAR-T persistence
citation: Neelapu SS et al. N Engl J Med 2017;377:2531-2544 (ZUMA-1, PMID 29226797)

trial: Post-approval case series (Seattle Children's and others)
outcome: Relapse as CD19-negative acute myeloid leukemia (lineage switch) sharing the founding clone and cytogenetics
resistance_mechanism: Lineage plasticity/transdifferentiation: KMT2A-rearranged blasts reprogram from lymphoid to myeloid, escaping CD19-directed therapy while retaining the leukemic clone
citation: Gardner R et al. Blood 2016;127:2406-2410 (PMID 26907630); Jacoby E et al. Nat Commun 2016;7:12320

outcome: On-target efficacy accompanied by severe and occasionally fatal cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and ICANS neurotoxicity
resistance_mechanism: On-mechanism toxicity: massive T-cell activation triggers an IL-6/IFN-gamma cytokine storm (CRS) and blood-brain-barrier disruption (ICANS); dose-limiting rather than an efficacy-resistance mechanism
citation: Maude SL et al. N Engl J Med 2018;378:439-448 (ELIANA); Neelapu SS et al. 2017 (ZUMA-1)

outcome: Higher CR than chemotherapy but frequent relapse; notable veno-occlusive disease (VOD/SOS); CD22 loss at relapse
resistance_mechanism: CD22 antigen escape (reduced surface density, epitope loss, isoform switching); plus on-mechanism hepatic sinusoidal obstruction limiting subsequent transplant
citation: Kantarjian HM et al. N Engl J Med 2016;375:740-753 (INO-VATE, PMID 27292104)

outcome: Phase 3: PFS improved but OS was HARMED with increased mortality (mostly fatal infections) in the unselected population; benefit confined to t(11;14)/BCL2-high myeloma
resistance_mechanism: Population mismatch: only BCL2-dependent myeloma (t(11;14)) responds, while unselected/high-BCLXL-MCL1 disease derives no survival benefit and suffers on-mechanism infection mortality; canonical unstratified-population failure
citation: Kumar S et al. Lancet Oncol 2020;21:1630-1642 (PMID 33129376)

trial: Phase 2 siltuximab + bortezomib (and front-line VMP study)
outcome: Phase 2 negative: no PFS (8.0 vs 7.6 mo) or OS benefit added to bortezomib despite IL-6's role in myeloma biology; the front-line VMP combination (NCT00911859) was likewise negative
resistance_mechanism: IL-6 is a supportive microenvironmental correlate, not a non-redundant survival driver; blockade is compensated by alternative cytokines (IGF-1, APRIL) and NF-kB signaling
citation: Orlowski RZ et al. Am J Hematol 2015;90:42-49 (PMID 25294016); San-Miguel J et al. Blood 2014;123:4136 (PMID 24833354)

target_mechanism: Kinesin spindle protein (KSP/Eg5) inhibitor causing mitotic arrest
outcome: Modest single-agent ORR (~15-16%); did not advance to registration; efficacy limited by a pharmacologic biomarker
resistance_mechanism: Pharmacologic sequestration: high plasma alpha-1 acid glycoprotein (AAG) binds filanesib and lowers free drug, so only AAG-low patients respond; efficacy gated by a pharmacologic biomarker not used to select the broad population
citation: Shah JJ et al. Br J Haematol 2017;179:257-267 (PMID 28817190)

outcome: Highly active initially but near-universal acquired resistance in relapsed disease
resistance_mechanism: PSMB5 binding-site mutations and PSMB5 overexpression, upregulation of proteasome subunits, unfolded-protein-response bypass, and ABCB1-mediated drug efflux
citation: Oerlemans R et al. Blood 2008;112:2489-2499 (PMID 18541827)

outcome: Phase 3 negative: single-agent carfilzomib did not improve OS vs control (low-dose corticosteroids +/- optional cyclophosphamide) in advanced, heavily pretreated RRMM
resistance_mechanism: Cross-resistance in a proteasome-inhibitor-refractory population plus insufficiency of monotherapy without combination partners; control-arm/endpoint heterogeneity also limited detectable benefit
citation: Hajek R et al. FOCUS trial, Leukemia 2017;31:107-114 (PMID (verify - unresolved))

target_mechanism: Cereblon (CRBN) molecular glue driving IKZF1/3 degradation
outcome: Acquired IMiD refractoriness after initial response, a defining feature of relapsed myeloma
resistance_mechanism: CRBN downregulation, loss-of-function CRBN mutations/deletions, and CRBN-pathway (CUL4/DDB1) alterations abolish IKZF1/3 degradation, restoring IRF4/MYC
citation: Zhu YX et al. Blood 2011;118:4771-4779 (PMID 21860026); Kortum KM et al. Blood 2016

outcome: High response rate but nearly all patients relapse, some with BCMA antigen loss
resistance_mechanism: BCMA antigen escape via biallelic TNFRSF17 (BCMA) deletion/mutation and gamma-secretase-mediated BCMA shedding (soluble BCMA) reducing target density; also CAR-T exhaustion/loss
citation: Munshi NC et al. N Engl J Med 2021;384:705-716 (KarMMa); Da Via MC et al. Nat Med 2021;27:616-619

outcome: High response in triple-class-refractory myeloma but relapses occur via antigen and T-cell escape
resistance_mechanism: BCMA loss/mutation and soluble-BCMA sink reduce target engagement; T-cell exhaustion and an immunosuppressive TME blunt bispecific efficacy
citation: Moreau P et al. N Engl J Med 2022;387:495-505 (MajesTEC-1, PMID 35661166); Lee H et al. Nat Med 2023 (BCMA escape)

target_mechanism: Anti-SLAMF7 (CS1) monoclonal antibody driving NK-cell ADCC
outcome: No objective responses as monotherapy; efficacy realized only in combination with lenalidomide (later ELOQUENT-2)
resistance_mechanism: SLAMF7-directed ADCC is insufficient alone; requires lenalidomide-primed/activated NK cells for co-stimulation, so single-agent use lacked a working mechanistic rationale
citation: Zonder JA et al. Blood 2012;120:552-559, PMID 22184404

target_mechanism: Covalent BTK inhibitor of BCR signaling
outcome: Responses achieved but frequent primary and acquired resistance; post-ibrutinib MCL carries a poor prognosis
resistance_mechanism: Bypass of BTK via alternative/non-canonical NF-kB activation (NIK, BIRC3 or TRAF2/3 loss) and PI3K-AKT; less commonly BTK C481S; survival becomes BCR-independent
citation: Rahal R et al. Nat Med 2014;20:87-92 (PMID 24362935); Chiron D et al. Cancer Discov 2014;4:1022-1035

target_mechanism: Abbreviated dose-dense multiagent chemotherapy plus consolidative radiotherapy
outcome: Phase 3 negative: Stanford V was not superior to ABVD for failure-free or overall survival; ABVD remained the standard
resistance_mechanism: Regimen rearrangement/intensification without a new mechanistic target yields equivalent efficacy while adding toxicity and radiotherapy burden; no biological differentiator
citation: Gordon LI et al. J Clin Oncol 2013;31:684-691 (PMID 23182987)

outcome: Accelerated approval later withdrawn (2022): updated UNITY-CLL analysis showed an imbalance in deaths versus control, rendering benefit-risk unfavorable
resistance_mechanism: On-mechanism PI3K-delta class toxicity (immune-mediated and infectious deaths) producing an overall-survival detriment; the same class liability seen with idelalisib/duvelisib
citation: Gribben JG et al. UNITY-CLL; FDA/TG Therapeutics withdrawal 2022 (PMID (verify - unresolved))

target_mechanism: Peptide-drug conjugate delivering an alkylator payload via intracellular aminopeptidases
outcome: Phase 3: PFS endpoint met but an OS detriment vs pomalidomide (notably in prior-transplant/early-relapse patients) prompted an FDA safety alert and US withdrawal (later partial EU reinstatement)
resistance_mechanism: Population harm: the aminopeptidase-targeted alkylator conferred an OS detriment in prior-autotransplant patients, an unfavorable benefit-risk in an unstratified population
citation: Schjesvold FH et al. Lancet Haematol 2022;9:e98-e110 (OCEAN, PMID 35032434)

target_mechanism: Third-generation P-glycoprotein (ABCB1/MDR1) efflux-pump inhibitor intended to restore intracellular anthracycline/anthracenedione levels
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: no OS benefit; median OS 7.2 mo (zosuquidar) vs 9.4 mo (placebo), P=0.281 (n=449)
resistance_mechanism: P-gp overexpression is a marker of adverse-biology AML but pharmacologic pump inhibition did not translate to survival; MDR is multifactorial (multiple ABC transporters, apoptosis defects), so blocking one efflux pump is insufficient

sponsor: Cancer and Leukemia Group B (CALGB) / NCI
outcome: NEGATIVE / halted: ADEP arm closed after 120 pts for excessive early mortality; no benefit
resistance_mechanism: Valspodar inhibits CYP3A4, altering pharmacokinetics of co-administered cytotoxics and requiring dose reduction, causing on-mechanism toxicity that negated any MDR-reversal benefit

target_mechanism: P-glycoprotein (ABCB1/MDR1) efflux inhibition to reverse multidrug resistance
sponsor: Cancer and Leukemia Group B (CALGB) / NCI
outcome: NEGATIVE Phase 3: adding valspodar did not improve outcomes in younger AML patients
resistance_mechanism: P-gp inhibition alone does not overcome AML chemoresistance; efflux is one of several parallel resistance routes and PK interactions blunt benefit
citation: Kolitz JE et al. Blood 2010;116(9):1413-1421. PMID 20522709
